I am 65 years old and I have farmed these 8 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I went to middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bag labels and I understand what the extension people say, but I still trust my own eyes more than any paper. Last year I planted 5 mu as wheat-maize and 3 mu in cotton, and that worked fine. My wheat made about 1000 jin per mu and the maize made about 1100 jin per mu. The cotton price was not great but I still cleared some money. This year I will do the same because changing things is risky and I know this land.

For my wheat, I will rotary till the ground in early October and sow improved wheat seed — about 25 jin per mu. At sowing I will put down 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu, the 15-15-15 kind. Then in March, at green-up, I will topdress with 60 jin of urea per mu. Some people say that is a lot, but last year my wheat stalks were thick and the grain was plump, so I will not cut back. I would rather spend a little more on fertilizer than have thin stalks and low yield. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I will irrigate four times with my well: sowing water, winter water, jointing water, and grain-filling water. I will spray three times — herbicide once in early spring, then insecticide twice for aphids and powdery mildew.

For maize, after I harvest wheat in early June, I will not till. I will plant hybrid maize seed directly into the wheat stubble — about 5 jin per mu of Denghai or something similar from the seed dealer. I will put 80 jin of compound fertilizer in the seed furrow and then topdress with 50 jin of urea at the big trumpet stage. I will irrigate twice: once right after sowing if the soil is dry, and again at big trumpet. Three sprays total: one herbicide and two for corn borer and armyworm.

For cotton, I will rotary till 3 mu in late April. I will sow improved cotton seed, Guoxinmian, about 4 jin per mu. Basal fertilizer is 60 jin of compound fertilizer per mu, and I will add 40 jin of urea at flowering. Cotton pests are the worst — bollworm comes every year without fail. I will spray 12 times, mostly insecticide, starting in June and going every 7 to 10 days through August. I will irrigate twice: at flowering and at boll stage.

My son and daughter-in-law work in the factory in Handan, so they send money home. That helps with input costs. But fertilizer is expensive this year and the dealer raised prices again. Still, I will not reduce my rates. I watch Old Wang and Old Li next door — they are using about the same amounts on their wheat-maize fields, so I know I am in the right range. I have been doing this longer than most of them. I know my well never runs dry, I know this soil, and I know these crops. I will stick with what works.
